messages:
Maya G.: quick design ask — I'm doing a pass on the version history timeline in Deployments. The commit badges (sha + author) are visually dense and when you "expand" a version we read out a bunch of things that feel repetitive for screen readers. Suggestions for reducing noise?

Arjun S.: +1, saw that in user testing. Two quick ideas: 1) collapse author and time into one succinct line, 2) truncate sha to 7 chars and expose full on hover/focus.

Sam T.: agree with truncation. also thinking about compact layout: move badge group to the left rail and show only the primary label (e.g., "release/2026-04-11") in timeline rows. details pane can show commit/author/time. keeps timeline scan-friendly.

Priya L.: accessibility nit — screen readers currently announce: "expand details button, commit sha 0xabc... by John Doe, committed 3 hours ago, view diff" which is long. Proposal: for collapsed items announce: "Version: release/2026-04-11, committed 3 hours ago" and put the sha/author behind a secondary control with aria-expanded semantics. reduces verbosity while keeping info discoverable.

Maya G.: love that. How do folks feel about adding aria-live for rollout status changes (e.g., canary -> ramp -> full)? We had testers miss state changes when they happened quickly.

Arjun S.: aria-live polite for status chips should be fine. Important we de-dupe messages — only announce when state actually changes (not on every re-render). backend can emit an event id to gate announcements.

Sam T.: implementation note: we'll need a small JS util that compares previousStateId -> newStateId and pushes a single message to an offscreen live-region. I can draft a tiny hook. snippet: 

```js
// pseudo
useStatusAnnounce(prevId, nextId, label) {
  if (prevId !== nextId) {
    liveRegion.textContent = `${label} is now ${nextStateLabel}`;
  }
}
```

Priya L.: microcopy suggestion for the live announcement: use short actionable phrases e.g., "Canary rollout reached 10% traffic" vs "status changed to canary" — gives context without extra words. Also ensure announcements are localizable.

Maya G.: good call. UX copy: in the timeline rows, replace generic "details" CTA with contextual verbs — "View diff", "Open rollout chart", "Revert to this" depending on the available actions. That should help screen reader users and sighted users scanning CTAs.

Arjun S.: visual density question — should we keep the compact timeline default or let users toggle compact/comfortable? Preference from PMs was default compact with user-level preference saved.

Sam T.: toggle makes sense. We'll persist in user settings and respect reduced-motion / prefers-contrast for accessibility. Also: keyboard focus order — ensure timeline row keyboard focus lands on the primary action, not the expand chevron. keyboard users expect to open the most likely action.

Priya L.: keyboard note: when pressing Enter on a focused row we should expand details (not follow the primary action link). That's consistent with list semantics. Primary action should be reachable by Tab after expansion.

deploy-bot: deployment event: canary 1742 -> 10% at 2165432250 UTC

Maya G.: thanks bot. For copy: replace "canary" label in the UI with a tooltip that explains the term for non-technical users e.g., "Canary — a small percentage of traffic to validate this version". Short tooltip only on hover/focus.

Arjun S.: last UX ask — when we show version diffs in-line, don't collapse unchanged files behind accordions by default. In testing, people assumed collapsed meant no changes. Show file list with badges: added/modified/removed and collapse large unchanged hunks behind a small "show unchanged" button.

Sam T.: noted. I'll prototype the compact timeline + details panel with the accessible live-region hook and updated CTAs. Will share a link to a Loom with interactions.

Maya G.: awesome. Priya, can you review the prototype for screen reader flow? If you can sign-off or list remaining a11y todos, we'll include them in the handoff ticket.

Priya L.: will do. I'll test NVDA + VoiceOver and post results. Expect a short checklist: live-region phrasing, focus order, aria-labels for chevrons, and keyboard-only reveal of sha/author.

Maya G.: thanks all — I'll create the ticket with the specs and copy changes. :sparkles:
